analysis.authors_year: J. A. Cuesta-Albertos, A. Gordaliza and C. Matran, 1997
analysis.research_question: How to design new clustering procedures with emphasis on robustness properties by extending impartial trimming to k-means, and what are their consistency and theoretical properties?

Proof of existence of trimmed k-means using topological arguments and continuity results

Simulation study using bivariate normal mixture distributions with inner and outer contamination, implemented with a simulated annealing algorithm
main_findings: The optimal trimming function essentially coincides with the indicator function of a generalized ball (the union of k balls of the same radius) centered at the k-set.
Trimmed k-means induce a partition into k clusters, and each cluster center is the Phi-mean of its corresponding cluster.

Under continuity of the limit probability distribution and uniqueness of the trimmed k-mean, empirical trimmed k-means are strongly consistent (converging in Hausdorff distance almost surely along with the trimmed k-variation).
Simulations demonstrate that simulated annealing is effective for optimization, though low trimming levels can induce bias due to high-density zones near cluster boundaries.
assumptions: The penalty function Phi is continuous, nondecreasing, with Phi(0) = 0 and Phi(x) < infinity for all x.
The probability measure PX is continuous for consistency theorems.
A specified proportion alpha of data points is trimmed.
